subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` self-pause tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted tool with explicit cap, interruption, restart, and sandbox semantics?
rationale: The request adds a new model-facing core scheduling primitive across agent turns, gateway wake behavior, session state, and possible config/default surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent product/API boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the capability direction and require the implementation to target the originating session, prove interrupt/restart behavior, enforce caps, and keep sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep existing cron/session surfaces
options.body: Decline a new core tool for now and leave delayed work on cron, exec completion wakes, process polling, and `sessions_yield` where those paths already have ownership.

options.title: Narrow to an extension seam
options.body: Ask for plugin/runtime API work instead of a built-in default tool if maintainers want optional self-pause behavior outside the core model-facing surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the capability direction and require the implementation to target the originating session, prove interrupt/restart behavior, enforce caps, and keep sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent runtime, cron, and product-boundary history make this the strongest available routing owner for the product/API choice.
